question: Follow up on the detention of Saudi human rights defender Abdulrahman alKhalidi in Bulgaria

Abdulrahman al-Khalidi, a Saudi human rights defender, sought asylum in Bulgaria in October 2021 and has been detained at the Busmantsi Detention Centre for over four years. His asylum application was rejected, and a deportation order to Saudi Arabia is in place, where he faces serious risks such as possible execution due to his activism about breaches of prisoner’s rights.
A study by Parliament’s Subcommittee on Human Rights (DROI) published on 12 June 2025 highlighted his case as a key example of the use of detention in transnational repression. 1.

Does the Commission consider that extended detention in this case, and the risk of return to Saudi Arabia, comply with EU law, including the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union, the Reception Conditions Directive1, the Asylum Procedures Regulation2, and the Returns Directive3?
When was the last time the Commission visited the Busmantsi detention facility, and how frequently does the Commission conduct such visits?

If the Commission has recently visited the Busmantsi facility, what observations did it make and what follow-up actions does it intend to take to ensure Bulgaria’s practice aligns with EU standards on the treatment of detained asylum seekers and the principle of non-refoulement?

OJ L, 2024/1346, 22.5.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2024/1346/oj. OJ L, 2024/1348, 22.5.2024, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1348/oj. OJ L 348, 24.12.2008, pp. 98–107, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2008/115/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.1.2026) The applicable rules for granting international protection are laid down in Directive 2013/32/EU1, which refers to Directive 2013/33/EU2 on detention of applicants. The latter sets out grounds and safeguards for detention, without prejudice to other grounds under national law.

Under Directive 2008/115/EC (‘Return Directive’)3, Member States have the obligation to issue a return decision to illegally staying third-country nationals and to take all necessary and proportionate measures to ensure effective return. When other sufficient but less coercive measures cannot be applied effectively, it allows for detention for the purpose of removal.

These directives also set out safeguards to guarantee the protection of fundamental rights during the asylum and return processes, including refugee protection, the principle of nonrefoulement and human rights obligations, which Member States have to respect.

Member States are solely responsible for assessing applications for international protection and carrying out return, ensuring compliance with EU law, including the respect of fundamental rights. The Commission cannot intervene in assessing the merits of individual cases.

The Commission visited the Busmantsi facility in November 2025, as part of the Schengen evaluation of Bulgaria, to determine if the Bulgarian authorities implement pre-removal detention in line with EU requirements and standards. The outcome of the evaluation will be reflected in the 2025 Bulgaria Report, to be adopted in line with Regulation (EU) 2022/9224.
It will provide the Commission with a basis for engaging with Bulgaria on structural reforms, including, where necessary, matters related to the use of pre-removal detention.
1 Directive 2013/32/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013 on common procedures

for granting and withdrawing international protection (recast), OJ L 180, 29.6.2013, pp. 60-65, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2013/32/oj. 2 Directive 2013/33/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 26 June 2013 laying down standards for the reception of applicants for international protection (recast), OJ L 180, 29.6.2013, pp. 96-116, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2013/33/oj.

3 Directive 2008/115/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 December 2008 on common standards and procedures in Member States for returning illegally staying third-country nationals, OJ L 348, 24.12.2008, pp. 98–107, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2008/115/oj.

4 Council Regulation (EU) 2022/922 of 9 June 2022 on the establishment and operation of an evaluation and monitoring mechanism to verify the application of the Schengen acquis, and repealing Regulation (EU) No 1053/2013, OJ L 160, 15.6.2022, pp. 1-27, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/922/oj.
